assertions.name: confinement_lp_is_homogeneous
assertions.source: feasible(n) = n * feasible(1) as an identity on the constraint functions at 50 dps — the cone-slice structure of 1^T x = n with G x >= 0, checked without an LP solver

assertions.name: lp_objective_is_degenerate
assertions.source: min t.x = 0 and y0* = 0 at every tested n, so the optimal face is not a point and the LP does not pin x* — the offset is a solver artifact

description: Tests whether the confinement operator-selection LP's solution offset can carry theta_K. Two independent reasons it cannot. (1) The Frobenius constraint Gx >= 0 and the net constraint 1^T x = n are both homogeneous, so feasible(n) = n * feasible(1) as an IDENTITY (verified on the constraint functions at 50 dps, no solver); with t and G knot-independent and only n_target = |tr_M(K)| varying, two knots give parallel offsets, so the pair (magnitude, angle) is ratio-shaped and unfalsifiable by AfreeThetaConstraint.ratio_attained. (2) The objective is DEGENERATE: min t.x = 0 and y0* = 0 at every n, so the optimal face is not a point and x* is not determined by the LP — 'the offset' is a solver artifact. Supersedes this witness's earlier x*(n) = (n/n0)x*(n0) measurement, which read scipy/HiGHS's vertex selection rather than a property of the program. Escape: a formulation with knot-dependent t or G is not homogeneous and is not excluded. Nothing fitted.

data.program: min t.x s.t. 1^T x = n_target, G x >= 0 (prop:operator-selection-lp)

cone_slice_identity.method: (Gx)/n vs G(x/n) on 200 deterministic points with 1^T x = n, evaluated at 50 dps — no LP solver

lp_degeneracy.consequence: the optimal face is not a point, so x* and hence the offset are not determined by the LP; the returned point is a solver choice

lp_precision.why: the interior-point solver's convergence gap, not float arithmetic, is the accuracy floor; values are reported to 15 digits, inside it. The previous version solved this LP with scipy/HiGHS in float64 and published 17.

RETRACTED_measurement.why_retracted: solver-dependent, not a property of the LP. scipy/HiGHS crosses over to a basic (vertex) solution; vertices of n*P are n times vertices of P, so the scaling is reproduced by the solver's selection rule regardless of the program. clarabel, a pure interior-point method, returns a different point of the same zero-objective face and the same LP 'fails' the test.
RETRACTED_measurement.replaced_by: the cone_slice_identity block, which needs no solver

data.why_it_matters: homogeneity makes the offset direction knot-independent and the magnitude proportional to tr_M(K); the pair is therefore ratio-shaped and unfalsifiable by ratio_attained. Degeneracy makes the offset undefined in the first place.
data.the_only_escape: put the braid's operator content into the OBJECTIVE t or the GRAM G, not merely the net constraint n_target; that breaks homogeneity and is not excluded here
data.verdict: THE CONFINEMENT LP CANNOT CARRY ϑ_K, and the reason is stronger than the one this probe originally recorded. TWO FACTS, established separately. (1) HOMOGENEITY, now as an IDENTITY rather than a measurement: 1^T x = n and G x >= 0 are both homogeneous, so feasible(n) = n * feasible(1) exactly — checked on the constraint functions at 50 dps to 2.32e-69, with no solver involved. Since t and G are knot-INDEPENDENT (properties of the H_3 basis at q0) and only n_target = |tr_M(K)| varies, two knots give PARALLEL offsets: the ANGLE carries zero knot information and the MAGNITUDE is a fixed constant times tr_M(K), so the pair supplies ONE knot-dependent number and its content is the ratio tr_M(K1)/tr_M(K2). AfreeThetaConstraint.ratio_attained proves a ratio-shaped candidate is unfalsifiable. (2) WORSE: the objective is DEGENERATE. min t·x = 0 and y0* = 0 at every tested n (to 4.37e-16, the solver's duality gap), so the optimal face is not a point and the LP does not determine x* at all. 'The offset from the lattice saddle' is therefore not a well-defined function of the knot even before homogeneity is invoked — it is whatever point on a zero-objective face the solver happens to return. RETRACTED, and this is the reason the second fact surfaced: the earlier version reported x*(n) = (n/n0) x*(n0) to 1e-9 as the measurement establishing homogeneity. That number was an artifact of scipy/HiGHS crossing over to a VERTEX — vertices of n*P are n times vertices of P, so any vertex-returning solver reproduces the scaling regardless. Re-run against clarabel's interior point the same LP 'fails' it. The conclusion was right; the evidence was solver-dependent and has been replaced by the identity above. THE ESCAPE, unchanged and still the only one: a formulation whose t or G is itself knot-dependent is NOT homogeneous and is NOT excluded — the braid's operator content must enter the OBJECTIVE or the GRAM, not merely the net constraint. SCOPE (a): this excludes the canonical scalar-net formulation as the corpus builds it, not the proposal. Nothing fitted; nothing wired.
